changes: New Suncat-generated custom realms (map 999) use a deterministic 160 by 160 outdoor layout, 2.56 times the former tile area. A compact seed/region/road recipe travels with the authoritative server maze.

Four regions meld through warped, smooth biome weights: flower meadow near arrival, woodland, reed marsh and a rocky heath, alpine verge, dry scrub or overgrown ruins selected by the scenario theme. Winding roads and alternate approaches connect the refuge, outpost, encounters and distant keep.

Meadow art uses the existing pale flowers; woodland bell flowers, reeds with occasional marsh irises, low heath, alpine rosettes, sparse dry scrub and ruin plants use small cached procedural sprites. Plants mix near boundaries and remain off roads, pools, walls, the outpost, actor starting positions and major combat clearings.

Ground colors blend between regions in both 3D and overhead views. Two-tile ground patches split at solid/water borders; spatial buckets restrict work to the camera neighborhood. Plants follow the existing 720/520/360/220 budgets and reduced-motion setting, share depth sorting, and use existing layered world occlusion.

Six peaceful animals replace six extra hostile wanderers; scouts are distributed around the biome regions. Existing services, scenario quests, defenders, wildlife and combat use existing behavior. This pass does not add a new NPC intelligence model or increase the starting population.

Biome scenery is client-side decoration, with no NPC simulation, collision, target rings, item drops or individual network updates. A new instance or legacy custom map clears the scenery cache; saved generated realms keep their recipe and restore deterministically.

Map 777, Moors, Tintagel and general NPC distribution are unchanged. No dens, continent expansion or story rewrites. Lore Previous/Next at both chapter ends is preserved. Devlog displays v126; no external dependencies or assets added.

methods: 108 seed/theme combinations exercise the actual server generator, refuge, road/landmark reachability, unique reachable actor placement, near-arrival meadow, climate variants and deterministic repeatability.

Node/jsdom executes all 13 actual client scripts with stub canvas and an in-process simulated transport. It tests server-blueprint loading, local floor/plant selection, image-cache reuse, wall clipping calls, reduced graphics budgets, new instance/legacy resets, and fresh-runtime saved-realm resume.

An actual hostile NPC update loop crosses meadow terrain and reaches the normal player contact-attack callback while foliage is active. Damage resolution is intercepted in this controlled test; this is not a full combat balance/playthrough test.
